steps.title: Release a loaded hinge from rest
steps.explanation: Begin at 30° with a 2 kg point load, zero angular velocity and zero activation. Gravity contributes −4.53712 N m while passive muscle contributes only +0.393991 N m. There is no motor holding this forward simulation at its initial angle.
steps.observe: The initial net moment is negative, so the first motion must lower the arm. Activation is zero even though excitation is already 0.6.

steps.title: Force reversal does not instantly reverse velocity
steps.explanation: Advance five fixed RK4 steps, or 0.025 s. Activation has risen to 0.236082. The current muscle moment now exceeds gravity, but the arm retains negative velocity from its initial lowering; acceleration and velocity are different quantities.
steps.observe: Angle = 29.912° and angular velocity = −0.033263 rad/s, despite muscle moment +7.12093 N m versus gravity −4.52505 N m. Work-balance residual is about 3.19 × 10⁻⁷ J.

steps.title: Let the declared forces produce the lift
steps.explanation: Advance the same constant-excitation run to 0.30 s. The solver, rather than a pose slider, determines the angle and speed. Mechanical energy accounting includes signed active work, passive storage, gravity and damping exactly once in the stated continuous model.
steps.observe: Angle = 98.956°, activation = 0.598513 and angular velocity = 10.8734 rad/s. The numerical work-balance residual is about 2.27 × 10⁻⁵ J; these high speeds belong to the synthetic fixture.

steps.title: Change load, keep input and elapsed time
steps.explanation: Restart from the same 30° pose with a 5 kg load and the same excitation and 0.30 s endpoint. The heavier load changes both gravitational moment and rotational inertia. No controller secretly forces the previous trajectory.
steps.observe: Activation is still 0.598513, but angle is only 41.1118° and angular velocity 2.10467 rad/s. The different fiber length also changes tension; this is not a pure force-velocity law.

audit.finding: The adapter showed a moving angle and tension without the moment balance, angular velocity or energy residual needed to explain initial lowering and later lift. Excitation was hidden.
audit.change: Exposed excitation, individual moments, velocity, completed time, domain-stop flag and work residual; added the initial-pose reference line and controlled load comparison.
audit.remaining: Authored single hinge with rigid tendon and no joint-contact solve or measured force-velocity law. Domain exit retains the last admissible state; it is not a collision response. This sequence uses constant excitation; pulse/release remains in the full original lab.
